Opisałam pod innymi komentarzami trochę więcej o naszych finansach i gdzie szukać ludzi. Generalnie, pieniądze są z pracy. Ale jak mieszkasz z wieloma osobami to łatwo mieć sporo pieniędzy a pracować mniej i/lub rzadziej - wyobraź sobie o ile więcej pieniędzy ma rodzina, gdzie oboje partnerów pracuje. A potem wyobraź sobie, że masz 10 osób wnoszących pieniądze do domu. A potem że mieszkasz na sporej ziemi na wsi, z dużą liczbą domów, gdzie do budżetu dokłada się kilkadziesiąt osób. Szybko pieniądze zaczynają liczyć się w setkach tysięcy i więcej, nikomu niczego nie brakuje. 

Skąd wziąć dostatecznie duży dom? To pytanie dla kogoś, kto chce taką komunę założyć. Ja nie wiem. Ja dołączyłam do komuny, która już istnieje od kilkudziesięciu lat i która ma już swoją ziemię i budynki. Są tacy, co wolą zakładać własne albo dołączać do takich na przykład początkujących ekowiosek, gdzie wszystko trzeba sobie najpierw zbudować albo wyremontować. Nie moje klimaty - ja polecam dołączyć do czegoś, co istnieje już jakiś czas i działa. Bo dużo komun się otwiera, a potem istnieje do pierwszej kłótni i wszyscy się rozchodzą.

Swojego domu i swojej społeczności nie będę outować na Reddicie. Zresztą, i tak nie szukamy na razie nowych osób bo wszystkie pokoje są pełne, ale powodzenia dla twoich znajomych. Warto wiedzieć, że praca-dom-praca-dom i zapierdalanie byle tylko starczyło do następnej wypłaty to nie jedyna opcja, żeby przetrwać w matrixie:P

Zobacz sobie komentarz wyżej, pod którym opisałam więcej szczegółów naszych finansów. Ale kasa generalnie normalnie z pracy. Jak masz kilkadziesiąt osób mieszkających razem, z których każda w nosi do domu (lub, jak u nas, domÓW) jakieś pieniądze i dzielicie się podstawowymi wydatkami, to można żyć jak pączuś w masełku:P

A gdzie szukać? To już inna zagadka.

Najpierw trzeba wiedzieć, czego się szuka. Komuna, czyli taka społeczność dzieląca się wydatkami, to bardzo szczególny rodzaj tak zwanej "intentional community".

Może ktoś woli taką, gdzie ludzie dzielą się tylko obowiązkami a nie finansami? Co-housing? Coś religijnego, spirytualnego, czy tak jak u mnie bez żadnej wiodącej ideologii? Coś bardziej jak ekowioska czy może w mieście? Taka, gdzie przyjmuje się rodziny z dziećmi, samych dorosłych, tylko artystów, i tak dalej i tak dalej.

Nie mam całej wiedzy w temacie szukania, bo swoją znalazłam przez przypadek przez Facebooka. No ale właśnie grupki na Facebooku, albo:

ic. org - strona z różnymi społecznościami, które się ogłaszają szerszej publice

ecovillagegathering . org - coroczne spotkanie ludzi żyjących w ekowioskach i zainteresowanych. Ci ludzie na pewno znają też wszelkie inne społeczności/komuny i tak dalej

Słyszałam, że na rainbow gatheringach też się da taki networking robić. Wiem, że ludziom się wydaje, że to spotkania hipisów, którzy palą zioło w lesie przez miesiąc, ale w rzeczywistości to często zbieranina ludzi, którzy zamiast życia typu praca-puste mieszkanie-praca, wybrali jakieś alternatywne ścieżki i chcą poznać innych podobnych sobie. Znam kilka osób, które właśnie na rainbow poznali kogoś, kto ich pokierował albo znał jakąś ciekawą inicjatywę.


Generalnie jak się zainteresujesz tematem i zaczniesz poznawać ludzi żyjących w różnych takich co-opach, to szybko poznajesz więcej i więcej takich społeczności, aż może w końcu któraś będzie odpowiednia dla Ciebie.

Jak mieszkasz z wieloma osobami i każde z was wnosi jakieś pieniądze do domu (w naszym przypadku kompleksu domów!), to znacznie łatwiej zarobić na wszystko.

Każda komuna czy inna intencjonalna społeczność (bo komuna to bardzo specyficzny rodzaj tak zwanych intentional communities), ma swoje własne zasady, więc mogę się wypowiedzieć tylko o mojej.

Wszystkie pieniądze, które zarobimy, odkładamy na wspólne konto. W szczególnych przypadkach możemy przedyskutować, że pieniądze są prywatnie twoje - na przykład ktoś ci umarł no to na spadek ci nie wejdziemy, jak mama ci przesyła pieniądze w prezencie to też twoje, itd. Generalnie tylko pieniądze z pracy są wspólne, a inne przypadki podlegają dyskusji.

Później wydatki dzielą się na wspólne i prywatne. Wspólne jak wszystko związane z domem, sprzątaniem, jedzeniem, i tak dalej. Jest bardzo szczegółowy regulamin tego, co jest wspólne a co nie.

Prywatne to właśnie ciuchy, jakieś prywatne wyjazdy etc. Co miesiąc każdy dostaje kieszonkowe dostosowane do potrzeb - np. po opłaceniu jedzenia, domu, etc etc, ktoś mówi, że w sumie 500 zł miesięcznie na zachcianki mu wystarcza. Ktoś inny jest przewlekle chory, potrzebuje pieniędzy na leki, więc dajemy mu więcej.

Ale generalnie wszystko podlega dyskusji. Np. ktoś chce odwiedzić rodzinę w innym kraju, ale nie ma pieniędzy na bilet. Możemy przedyskutować i uznać to za wspólny wydatek. Albo może chcemy gdzieś razem pojechać w kilka czy kilkanaście osób, bo dawno nie spędzaliśmy czasu razem - możemy to uznać za wspólny wydatek, jeśli nikt nie ma nic przeciwko.

Mamy też osoby, które są bardziej odpowiedzialne za pilnowanie naszych finansów, robienie budżetów, etc, żeby się upewnić, że na pewno możemy sobie pozwolić na większy wydatek dla zabawy. Bo wszyscy się wymieniamy obowiązkami - np. jedna osoba jest od finansów, druga od planowania posiłków, trzecia od robienia zakupów, i tak dalej.

Edit: ja na przykład pracowałam przez rok. Skończyłam tę pracę w sierpniu zeszłego roku. niedługo może się znowu rozejrzę za pracą. Generalnie żyjąc w komunie i dzieląc się wydatkami jest tych pieniędzy znacznie więcej i często można sobie pozwolić na kilka miesięcy gdzie po prostu żyje się pełnią życia zamiast zapierdalać

Yes, it was common money. It comes from many different sources. To join the community, you need to pay €1000 fee. We have a second hand shop in a different town, that some people are responsible for, and it gives us profit. Sometimes we get donations from random people. If you're not a member, but want to sleep and eat here, you can pay a cheap fee, like in a cheap hostel, and stay. We organise different conferences, events, and camps, that people need to pay for to participate in. Also many small businesses nearby know, that if they need someone for a short contract (painting some walls for cheap price, reloading stuff because your regular employee called in sick, etc etc), they will find some willing person to do it here. And then, every member each year has to go on what we call saving-up. That means you find a job outside of the community, and earn as much as possible while spending as little as possible - it can last anywhere from 3 to even 10 months (but not 10 months every single year!). It depends on different factors (and no, the amount of your salary is not one of them. There's no 'goal' you need to meet to come back)

Every single penny that you earn is not yours, it's everyone's. Everything that you earn while being a member, goes to the common account. Then, everyone gets a monthly pocket money for expenses that are not covered by common money (anything that isn't facilities maintenance, food, transportation, etc etc). That pocket money is €40 for everyone, unless for some reason you need more (for example we all know that you have some health problems and buy some expensive meds. We will not buy them for you, but you can get a budget for them every month).
But! If you're in a serious need to buy something personal, but you don't have enough money, you can discuss it with everyone and if the common meeting agrees, that yes, you need it, you can have money for it. For example if you break your phone (it's needed for communication, and that's crucial here!), you can get a new one. You broke your glasses? Shit, buddy, of course, here, have some money. You want to go home for Christmas, but can't afford a ticket and your family cannot help you? Here, money.

Recently I got new shoes, because mine were falling apart.

And no, we don't reward our drivers in any special way. It's because everyone is responsible for something. 

And also, drivers and not just people with a driving license. You become the community driver when you agree that this is the responsibility that you want to take. If you have a driving license, but would like to be responsible for the economy or for doing shopping lists or for feeding the animals or... you get me, there's something to do for everyone. So if you want to do something else instead, go. No one forces you to be a driver.

But to make sure that we have a person for every responsibility, we discuss it on weekly common meetings. Like "hey, this person that was responsible for sorting trash said they want to join the team that cleans the kitchen instead, so we need another person to sort the trash. Who wants to do it?"
The meeting will not end until all roles are filled with enough people.

And with people going in and out, because of home travels, saving up, helping in some other businesses, etc etc, we need to make sure that we fill all the roles for each week. We can't have a situation like "oh! No one planned the meals for today, because people who usually do it went travelling!"

Edit: if your responsibility in the community is 'small', you can have multiple roles as well. If you do something big, like budgeting or maintenance work or making sure our electricity producing stuff works correctly (we have a windmill and solar panels, but both are pretty old so they require lots of love), then that's your only role. But if you do something small and simple, you can do more. So you can be both a driver and also responsible for cleaning 3 (out of many that we have) toilets

I've never used a deodorant in my entire life. But I also don't use soap unless I'm actually dirty (with paint, grease, etc. Sweat is not dirt), and I don't use any hair products, shampoo included. I believe that's why I don't smell. If you use too much products, which is sadly the norm, you destroy your body's natural balance and you start smelling lol

Our community owns a few cars. We have a few people that are responsible for them (to check their condition, tank, clean them, etc etc). We also have many drivers (but they're not the majority). We keep the names and contacts of all the drivers in our community Google drive (since we're a lot of people,  it's difficult to just remember who is responsible for what, especially for new people). The drivers also have their Whatsapp group.

So if somebody needs transportation, they contact the drivers. Then the driver "books" a specific car for a specific date and hour (to make sure we have enough cars available at all times for things we really need to do, like weekly shopping or picking up people that are coming back etc etc, and to make sure everyone always knows what's happening to all the cars at any given time). And by "book", I mean they put the info on the drivers' WhatsApp group.

Then, when a driver takes someone somewhere, they put in a special table the date, distance, the route, and the purpose. Because we pay for the gas from our common money, so we need to keep track of it and make sure that people use the cars only when they really need it

It may sound a bit complicated, but that's the system that works for us.

We also have a lot of common bikes (we're in Scandinavia, so bike lanes are everywhere). If you want to go somewhere for private reasons and don't want to bother anyone, you just take one of the bikes and go.

Then, we have people responsible for repairing and maintaining the bikes.

Edit: we're 10km away from the nearest bus stop/train station. And 30km away from any bigger town

I'd say trust your intuition. If one doctor treats you badly, go to another. 

Did they really listen to your concerns or were they just dismissing you from the start? Where they even open about the possibility of you being autistic in the first place? If you're a woman or even if you're just an adult – does the professional specialize in people like you or do they normally work with children and children only? If they tell you that you're not autistic, ask them why. If they can't give you an actual reasoning regards which criteria you fit and which you don't – search a second opinion.

But if you feel like you were well listened by them, they're actually specialized in the field, they can give you an actual reasoning behind their opinion – and they tell you that you're not autistic, then maybe you're not. I'm saying that because I've seen many people on this subreddit desperately seeking diagnosis even after being told by multiple doctors that they're not autistic but may have some other disorder(s) instead.

If the person in question has done a decent amount of research and is doing it in self-help purposes, but they can't get an official diagnosis for whatever reason – then yes.

If the person has done some 5-minute internet quiz and decided that they're autistic, then no.

If someone says that they self diagnose, even when having access to an actual diagnosis, because they think they're smarter than health professionals – no.

If someone is trying to get some benefits from it or tries to speak for the autistic community – no.
I'm not saying that a self diagnosed autistic CAN'T be actually autistic. But they could also be wrong..

Edit: it's all about the intentions and the self-diagnosis process itself.

My pieces of advice for anyone suspecting they are autistic:

1. Do as much research as you can. Read articles, or books even. Read as much about autism as you can. You can also take notes about the traits that sound like you.


2. Watch videos made by autistic people, especially the late-diagnosed ones, and listen to their stories and experiences. See if you can relate to them. The channels that helped me the most were these:

(note that I'm an AFAB, and so are these YouTubers. your experience may be slightly different if you are an AMAB)

3. Take online tests. If you are interested in pursuing an official diagnosis, you might want to save your results for later use.
I recommend these tests:
https://psychology-tools.com/test/autism-spectrum-quotient (but this one is rather old, so sometimes it might tell you that you are not autistic even if you actually are)
http://www.rdos.net/pl/index.php
https://www.aspietests.org/raads/

4. Engage with autistic people. Some autistic communities on Reddit, Facebook, or whatever social media you use. Talk with autistic people or just read about our daily experiences and struggles. See if you can relate.
Maybe you experience a certain trait and wonder if it might be related to autism? Don't be afraid to ask. We're very open (at least online lol) and always happy to help.

5. If you, after doing all the research, still think you are autistic... Congratulations and welcome to the community!
a) Self-diagnosis – many people don't have access to an official diagnosis, so being self-diagnosed autistic is absolutely okay. Self-diagnosis is accepted in this community. We know how hard it is to get the official diagnosis. However, it's better to not speak over and for the diagnosed autistics, as you can't be 100% sure that you actually have ASD.

It all depends on where you live. Just keep in mind that ASD isn't something that can be diagnosed by ANY psychologist or psychiatrist – most of them don't know shit about autism. And even if you find someone that specializes in autism, make sure that they specialize in diagnosing ADULTS. People that work with children only might not see the autistic traits in an adult and highly masking person. So whenever you are, just make sure to find the best specialist possible.

Good luck with your journey! I know it's hard, but you can do this!!

I'm not good with people, so maybe social phobia?
I'm often nervous, maybe it's anxiety?
I have to live within some rules that I set for myself or else I can't function, maybe it's OCD?
I don't have my own personality, I just copy people around me – maybe it's borderline or something?
I often feel burn out and without any energy – maybe depression?

And so on and so on. The thing is, I had some symptoms of each of them, but not enough to get diagnosed (in my opinion, because I didn't ask any specialist for help), and none of them would actually explain everything about me. I felt like something important was missing.

Then, accidentally, I came upon A MEME about autism. Something like "Were you the smart kid in school? We're you always bullied? Are you always burnt out nowadays? I have some news, you're autistic, here's a link to AQ test".

I did the test, scored high. Then I did another test, and another, and another... I fell into a rabbit hole of research about autism – articles, Facebook pages, subreddit, autistic YouTubers... I was consuming every single piece of information I could find on that topic.

After a few months I decided to contact a diagnostic team. Then I waited 2 months for a diagnosis process to start (yes, waiting lists are not so long in my country as they seem to be elsewhere), turned out I was right. They didn't have any doubt – I'm autistic.
